title: Interpersonal Theory of Mind Processing Pipeline
objective: Process bounded human-interaction text into an evidence-bounded external-state, internal-hypothesis, and recursive-epistemic analysis without converting inference into fact.

deterministicSemantics.rule: Deterministic structure does not imply objective access to private mental states.

epistemicLevels.label: L1
epistemicLevels.definition: What Actor A appears to believe, want, fear, know, or intend.

epistemicLevels.label: L2
epistemicLevels.definition: What Actor A appears to believe Actor B believes, wants, fears, knows, or intends.

epistemicLevels.label: L3
epistemicLevels.definition: What Actor A appears to want Actor B to believe about Actor A's own belief, intention, knowledge, or stance.

frameworks.name: Dennett's Intentional Stance
frameworks.use: Model an actor as operating from beliefs, desires, information, incentives, constraints, and internal logic.
frameworks.guardrail: Explanatory stance only; do not treat inferred beliefs/desires as established private facts or assume perfect rationality.

frameworks.name: Fonagy Mentalization Model
frameworks.use: Assess evidence of successful or failed attempts to represent another person's mental state.
frameworks.guardrail: Use observed mentalization quality / possible failure language; do not make a clinical diagnosis.

frameworks.name: Rogers Congruence
frameworks.use: Compare observed external presentation with the best-supported hypothesized internal operational state.
frameworks.guardrail: Ordinal evidence-bounded assessment unless a separate quantitative scoring model has been explicitly defined.

heuristics.label: Concrete vs. Abstract Rumination
heuristics.positiveDefinition: Concrete processing stays specific, testable, bounded, actionable, and revisable.
heuristics.flagDefinition: Abstract rumination globalizes into difficult-to-test questions about character, intent, permanent defect, destiny, or meaning without producing new evidence or action.

heuristics.label: Manufactured Obligation
heuristics.flagDefinition: Unsolicited, substitutionary, exaggerated, or strategically reframed help is used to generate unearned guilt, gratitude, debt, or compliance.

heuristics.label: Totalitarian Guardrails
heuristics.flagDefinition: Absolute conversational rules function to preclude contrary evidence, redefine disagreement as disloyalty/pathology, or immunize a fixed narrative from revision.
exclusions: procedural constraints unless used to suppress relevant divergent evidence

heuristics.label: Imposter Morality / Sociopathic Self-Image
heuristics.flagDefinition: The subject's own words or strongly contextualized behavior support a self-image in which positive traits, empathy, generosity, or morality are interpreted as calculated performance masking an inherently malicious or defective self.
heuristics.guardrail: Self-image pattern only; never diagnose sociopathy, psychopathy, ASPD, or another mental-health condition.

passes.title: External State Isolation
passes.prohibition: Do not infer motive in this pass.

passes.title: Internal State Approximation
passes.rule: Generate evidence-bounded hypotheses only after the external evidence ledger exists.

passes.title: Epistemic Layering
passes.rule: Track only recursive levels supported by the text, up to depth 3.

sections.title: Recursive Mind-Map (Epistemic Chain)
sections.format: Indented hierarchy using L1/L2/L3 where supported.

sections.title: Structural Blind Spots & Reasoning Flaws
sections.format: Bulleted index with evidence basis or explicit insufficient-evidence statement.

heuristicFamily.label: TheraminTrees-inspired modalities
heuristicFamily.guardrail: Do not treat these labels as validated psychiatric constructs, diagnoses, or automatic moral verdicts.

decisionPressureAndMoralContext.tragicDecisionStructure: Flag when every option reasonably perceived by the actor carried serious cost. This does not imply equal moral quality across options.
governingRules: Behavior under coercion or severe constraint is not equivalent to agreement.

minimalRecursionRule: Use the lowest recursive depth sufficient to explain the interaction. L2 and L3 each require independent evidence.
